newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian 88's Morrison shares stay halted.
newsitem.headline: Canadian 88's Morrison shares stay halted.

text.p: A cease-trade in Morrison Petroleums Ltd shares held by Canadian 88 Energy Corp and affiliated West Central Capital Corp will remain in effect until the company satisfies regulators its reasons for scrapping a takeover bid for Morrison are genuine, the Ontario Securities Commission ruled on Monday.

Canadian 88 said last weekend it withdrew its C$652 million hostile offer because it received new information from oil scouts that a much-watched Morrison natural gas well in southwestern Alberta would likely be dry or yield little gas.
The data showed Morrison was less valuable, it said.
Morrison said on Sunday it had no information that would back up the claim and that it concluded Canadian 88 dropped the offer over uncertainty regarding a hearing into alleged securities breaches.

"What the commission came back with was a decision that said they found Canadian 88's reasons for terminating their bid somewhat disingenuous," OSC general counsel Cathy Singer said in a phone interview from Toronto.

"(The commission) said the cease-trade will remain outstanding until the earlier of Friday or 48 hours after Canadian 88 satisfies staff of both the Ontario and Alberta commissions of the reasons for the termination."
Trading in the shares related to the bid were first ordered halted by regulators late Thursday.
Morrison vice-president of finance Paul Charron said on Monday that his company's lawyers were also of the view that Canadian 88's reasons for the move were "disingenuous."

Meanwhile, the Alberta and Ontario securities commissions said on Monday they would continue investigations into pre-bid trading of Morrison stock by Canadian 88 and West Central. No deadline to reach a decision was set.
